purpose: External (non-brand) audience voice for FLA project Phase 2.5 — what real people say about language anxiety, independent of any specific brand's marketing

by_source.telegram_discussion_chats: NOT FOUND (only brand-broadcast channels accessible via t.me/s/, no user discussion)

sample_quotes.text: I panic when I have to respond
Speaking out loud can cause a freeze response, a blank mind, or even physical symptoms: sweating, trembling, dizziness. Not because of the language — but because of the loss of control it represents.
When the Teacher asks something suddenly, I panic. I might know the [word] but…
sample_quotes.platform: Frontiers in Education research study (verbatim learner quote)

sample_quotes.text: They stay silent. They wait until they're 'perfect'. And they never speak.
I know so many people who refuse, or are scared, to use their English knowledge because they say they are not perfect.
Aiming for perfection was hard. It gave me a false sense of achievement and stirred up destructive spirals of self-doubt and self-loathing that eroded my mental health and held up real progress.
I understand everything… but I just can't speak
sample_quotes.platform: French Creative Academy blog (composite of learner reports)

sample_quotes.text: I am still struggling to understand when people are speaking to each other in Spanish. But when they talk to me directly… I get about one in four or five words.
You may feel like you understand a language but cannot speak when you interact with native speakers because you're unable to articulate yourself as well as you'd like to.
sample_quotes.platform: sarahvigil.com blog (paraphrasing learners she works with)

sample_quotes.text: some people are very good learners — but only in silence. They write, read, listen, but avoid speaking. Why? Because speaking is unpredictable. It demands speed, spontaneity, and letting go.
We can make excuses for why we don't want to speak, like saying that we're too embarrassed to speak or we are exhausted anyway
При разговоре с англоговорящим собеседником мы так боимся показаться глупыми или смешными, что предпочитаем молчать или говорить только Yes или No
a family culture of high expectations: You have to be excellent, or it's not worth trying. This creates perfectionism, and a deep fear of not being enough — especially when speaking.
Sometimes, language blocks are linked to older emotional stories: Not being listened to as a child, Being told to 'be quiet', Speaking in a family where expressing emotion was dangerous
Если в школе вас дразнили за произношение или на курсах иностранного языка преподаватель строго исправлял каждую ошибку, мозг запомнил: 'Говорить = стресс'
other people will judge their accents, laugh at their mistakes, and notice the inaccuracies.
А вдруг я буду долго подбирать слова, говорить медленно и с паузами. Иностранец подумает, что я глупый
главный враг в разговоре на английском — это боязнь «ляпнуть что-нибудь не то»
My accent is holding me back. People will judge me if I mess up.
Your accent is a reflection of your journey, your experiences, and the languages you've spoken. It's not something to hide; it's something to embrace.

Я перестала стесняться своего акцента после того, как переехала в Великобританию и своими ушами услышала все разнообразие местных акцентов... С акцентом говорят все — нет никакого смысла избавляться о
if you appear nervous, the listener is going to want to spare you the anxiety and will switch to English
I've learned how to appear cool as a cucumber even if my knee caps are shaking
We live in a place where locals do not tolerate a poor attempt at their language
The reason why I don't understand English now as much as I could is because of my laziness and lack of consistency.
Это не лень и не 'нет таланта к языкам'. Это отсутствие регулярной speaking practice
Языковой барьер — это не отсутствие знаний, а боязнь их использовать, если они далеки от идеала
С ней очень комфортно учиться, она спокойно и понятно объясняет, поддерживает и помогает не бояться

key_findings: RU and EN voices share IDENTICAL core themes (stupor/freeze, comprehension gap, perfectionism, accent shame, school trauma) — FLA is universal, not RU-cultural

RU-specific intensity: word 'ступор' is canonical and ubiquitous — no exact EN equivalent ('freeze' is closest). The Russian discourse explicitly names a phenomenology that EN sources describe more diffusely

Antishkola/YT/IG comments yielded ZERO FLA-relevant voices despite 100+ comments scanned — fan/lifestyle audience, not bleeding-from-the-block. This means audience pain language must come from EDUCATIONAL/forum spaces (4brain, englex, vc.ru), not from competitor comment sections
RU audience uses MORE somatic language: 'дрожащий голос, потные ладони, пустота в голове', 'красне', 'киваю', 'молчу'. EN sources more cognitive: 'blank mind', 'tongue-tied', 'frozen'
RU pain naming: 'молчаливый багаж' (silent baggage) is a magnificent native metaphor — found in englex.ru. Strong copy potential
RU motivation framing: 'на созвоне ты всё понимаешь, киваешь, потом злишься' (vc.ru) — WORK-MEETING-SHAME is the dominant RU JTBD context, NOT travel/dating (which dominates EN forums)

Universal pattern across both langs: 'I'll start speaking AFTER I learn X' — perpetual deferral. RU canonical: 'Сначала выучу все времена, потом заговорю'. EN canonical: 'They wait until they're perfect. And they never speak.'

ru_specific: Word 'ступор' as canonical concept — no equivalent in EN
Work-call shame ('на созвоне ты всё понимаешь, киваешь') as dominant adult context
Soviet/post-Soviet school trauma reference (called to blackboard, strict error correction)
en_specific: Stronger explicit mention of dating/relationships as motivator
More references to childhood emotional trauma as root cause (monoglotanxiety.com)
